C1585.title: Remote Provisioning Risks in eSIM/iSIM and SIM Swap Attacks
C1585.summary: An empirical study reveals how eSIM technology introduces new privacy and security risks through remote provisioning. The research finds that travel eSIMs often route user data through third-party networks, and opaque provisioning processes may allow attackers to exploit remote management features for SIM hijacking, leading to mobile service takeover and identity theft.

references.title: {eSIMplicity} or {eSIMplification}? Privacy and Security Risks in the {eSIM} Ecosystem
